findings.evidence: `grep -rn cross_commute TauCeti` gives exactly three hits: the definition at `JordanChevalley/Commuting.lean:56` and the two uses at `:149` and `JordanDecomposition/Commuting.lean:132`. `mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Commute/Defs.lean:97,103` define `Commute.mul_right` and `Commute.mul_left`, both tagged `@[to_additive (attr := simp)]`. The module docstring (lines 25–43) lists only the `LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.*` declarations, not this one.
findings.fix: Delete the declaration and inline the term at its two call sites (`TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/JordanChevalley/Commuting.lean:149` and `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/JordanDecomposition/Commuting.lean:132`): `((commute_semisimplePart_unipotentPart g).mul_left (commute_unipotentPart_semisimplePart_of_commute hgh).symm).mul_right ((commute_semisimplePart_unipotentPart_of_commute hgh).mul_left (commute_semisimplePart_unipotentPart h))`. If a named lemma is wanted, it belongs in the `Commute` namespace in a general algebra file, the way `TauCeti.Units.coe_inv_mem_adjoin` lives in `TauCeti/RingTheory/Adjoin/Unit.lean`.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.commute_mul_mul_of_cross_commute` is a general `Semigroup` fact with no Jordan content, exported publicly from a Jordan–Chevalley file under the bare `TauCeti` namespace (so no `Commute` dot-notation), and it is absent from the file's own `## Main declarations` list. Its whole proof is `(hac.mul_left hbc).mul_right (had.mul_left hbd)`, i.e. two applications of Mathlib's `Commute.mul_left`/`Commute.mul_right` (both `@[simp]`).

summary: The Jordan-side surface is minimal and complete, but the PR also exports a general-purpose Semigroup commutation lemma in the bare `TauCeti` root namespace from a Jordan–Chevalley module, where no consumer will find it and where it is undocumented; it is a one-term composition of two Mathlib simp lemmas.
